chapter_summary: Jesus teaches in the temple amid accusation and conflict. He shows mercy to an accused woman, calls himself the light of the world, promises freedom through truth, confronts sin and falsehood, and declares that he existed before Abraham.
main_lesson: Jesus brings light, truth, mercy, and freedom from sin, and his authority comes from the Father.

memory_verse.kjv: Then spake Jesus again unto them, saying, I am the light of the world: he that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
memory_verse.little_bible: Again, therefore, Jesus spoke to them, saying, “I am the light of the world. He who follows me will not walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life.”

parent_guide: Access: ages 9–12 with adult guidance; Parent Mode for sexual accusation, threatened stoning, death, suicide language, slavery imagery, demon accusations, ethnic insult, and attempted killing. John 7:53–8:11 is absent from the earliest surviving manuscripts and appears elsewhere in some later manuscripts, so its original location is uncertain. “The Jews” here identifies particular interlocutors, not all Jewish people; Jesus and his first followers were Jewish. Reject the Samaritan ethnic insult. Verse 22 mentions suicide; seek immediate qualified help if a child expresses self-harm thoughts. Do not use this chapter to silence reports, force reconciliation, minimize slavery, justify prejudice, or promise escape from harm.
application_for_children: Children may reject public shaming and prejudice, ask safe adults for help, and seek truth without obeying unsafe demands.
